title: Lesson 6: Number Splitting
subtopics: Addition by splitting into two easy chunks
Choosing the split line to avoid carries
Division by splitting into two sections
Division with three sections and longer numbers
learningGoals: Split a long calculation into smaller mental chunks.
Choose split points that reduce carries, borrowing, or awkward division.
Use number splitting across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
coreIdeas: A split is useful only when each chunk becomes easier than the whole problem.
Read the chunk answers from left to right so place value stays correct.
When a quotient chunk needs two places, keep the zero instead of dropping it.

workedExamples.question: How does 2345 + 6738 become 9083 by splitting?
workedExamples.method: Split both numbers as 23/45 and 67/38. Add the right chunk first: 45+38=83. Then add the left chunk: 23+67=90. Read the answer from left to right as 9083.

workedExamples.question: Why is 5454 - 1726 easy to split?
workedExamples.method: Split the numbers as 54/54 and 17/26. The right chunk gives 54-26=28 and the left chunk gives 54-17=37. Because no borrowing crosses the split, the answer reads as 3728.

workedExamples.question: Work 604 * 7 by splitting the number first.
workedExamples.method: Split 604 as 6/04. Multiply each chunk by 7: 6*7=42 and 04*7=28. Keep both places in the second chunk and read the answer as 4228.

workedExamples.question: Why does 612 / 6 become 102 when split?
workedExamples.method: Split 612 as 6/12. Divide each chunk by 6: 6/6=1 and 12/6=2. The second chunk must keep two places, so it is written as 02. Read the answer as 102.

starterPractice: Warm-up: split 2345 + 6738 after two digits and say the two chunk results aloud.
Carry choice: compare two possible split lines for 4554 + 3636 and choose the one that avoids a carry crossing the split.
Subtraction and multiplication: solve 5454 - 1726 and 814 * 4 by chunking before you calculate.
Division practice: solve 612 / 6 and 2849 / 7, keeping the zero when a quotient chunk needs two places.

screenplay.teacherLine: Review round! Addition by number splitting — break each number at the tens boundary, add the parts, then combine. Let us drill until it feels completely automatic!

screenplay.subtopic: Lesson Wrap-Up
screenplay.teacherLine: You completed Number Splitting. You split addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division into smaller parts and learned when place value forces you to keep a zero in the answer.

screenplay.checkpointPrompt: What must you preserve when a quotient chunk looks smaller than its place value?
screenplay.fallbackHint: You must preserve the full place width, including a zero when needed.

teachingFlowStages.intent: Open with a hard-looking sum and make it smaller by drawing a split line on the board.
Explain how chunking preserves place value and why a good split avoids carries or awkward borrowing.
Model one worked example each from addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
Ask the learner for the next chunk result before the full answer is revealed.
Move from easy two-chunk questions to longer splits and zero-sensitive quotient cases.
Confirm that every chunk answer fits back into the full number correctly.
Require the learner to explain where the split line was chosen and why it helped.
